transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I suppose occupational health sent me because... I've gotten into this pattern where I push breakfast and lunch aside. Usually it's during my long lab runs or exhibition work. And then, by the time I actually do sit down to eat, I keep it to something very small and controlled. So, they wanted me to come in and speak with you about it.

During these times when you are eating very little, do you ever find yourself having episodes where you feel you lose control and eat a much larger amount of food than most people would in a similar situation?

No, I don't really have anything like that. When I do finally eat, like I said, it's just a very small, specific amount. I don't ever feel like I lose control or eat a large amount of food at once. It's always very measured.

Do you find that your decision to limit your food intake is driven by a strong desire to lose weight or a fear of gaining weight, or is it more about a lack of interest in eating or discomfort with the sensory qualities of food?

It's definitely a fear of gaining weight. It doesn't have anything to do with a lack of interest or the sensory qualities of the food. 

Honestly, if the scale goes up even a fraction, I feel this... this sharp panic that I’m losing the discipline I’ve worked so hard to maintain. It's very important to me to keep things strictly controlled so that doesn't happen. So, yes, it's very much driven by that fear.
How do you feel when you look at your body in the mirror or think about your physical shape?

Well, when I look in the mirror, like before heading into the lab for the day, I don’t really see someone who is thin. I mostly just zero in on my stomach or my hips. It makes me feel as if those areas make me look careless, or just... unserious.
Could you tell me how much you currently weigh and how tall you are?

I'm five foot five. As for my weight, I don't have the exact number in my head right this second, but the numbers have kept drifting down. 

My clothes are definitely looser now. But, honestly, part of me sees that as a sign that I’m focused. It makes me feel like I'm not letting the chaos at work spill over into my body.
Could you tell me what your current weight is, or if you aren't sure, could you describe how much weight you have lost over the past few months?

I really don't know my exact weight right now. I don't weigh myself every day. But I've probably lost around... maybe 15 or 20 pounds over the last three or four months. I just know my pants from last year are falling off me, so I had to buy smaller ones for work.
